title: Electron Shell
summary: An Electron desktop task runner using suspending IPC channels, command state with refetch, and lifecycle-safe event subscriptions through @octanejs/electron.

journeys.title: Boot into the task index and report which IPC bridge answered
Read a task manifest and stream one run through to its completion line
Keep each task's streamed log to the selection that produced it
Recover the suspended task index after its first command rejects
Recover a rejected task manifest through the command's own refetch
Drop every line emitted while the log subscription is detached, then resume cleanly
Reflect native theme and window state through the desktop hooks
Exercise app, dialog, clipboard, and shell helpers from the renderer
Surface a refused run_task without leaving the log running, then run again

faultScenarios.description: The fault=list URL rejects the first list_tasks call, routes it to the @catch fallback, and reloads the index when the boundary is reset.
The fault=describe URL rejects the first describe_task call, surfaces it as command state rather than a thrown boundary, and recovers on refetch.
Disabling the watcher mid-run unsubscribes the Electron IPC listener, so the remaining lines and the completion line are never delivered.
The fault=run URL rejects the first run_task call, keeps the run panel Idle with an alert, and lets a second Run stream normally.
